The parent's own stages DM.0-DM.8 run from additive polynomials and Drinfeld modules through t-modules, L-values and periods to algebraic independence, and stop short of multiple zeta values in positive characteristic and Thakur's basis, which is what this route adds.

notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-7b31c4 (issue #1380). cc-fb70e5 appears nowhere in its files.

Provenance. The recorded e-print hash matches byte for byte: 6336dfc5...0c52de for the arXiv v2 source (a single gzipped Basis_Submit_v2.tex, 2086 lines). The extraction records no hash for the published Cambridge version, which is right: Cambridge Core watermarks each download with the requesting IP and a timestamp, so no such hash would be reproducible. I read the published text for the checks that needed it.

Numbering, which is the delicate part here. The class hangs every statement environment on the equation counter (\newtheorem{theorem}[equation]{Theorem} and so on) with \numberwithin{equation}{subsection}, so numbered displays consume numbers alongside statements and a simulation has to count align lines minus \notag as well as theorem environments. Doing that gives 43 numbered statements and reproduces the extraction's numbers exactly, Theorem 1.2.4 (the main theorem, label T:Main Thm) and Remark 1.2.5 among them. My first pass mislabelled the appendix as a sixth section because I had not handled \appendix; with that fixed the appendix statements come out A.1.1, A.1.2, A.2.3, A.3.1, A.3.2, A.3.7, A.3.8, exactly the numbers the extraction's locators use.

The extraction's dual numbering is real and correctly recorded: the preprint numbers by subsection and the published version by section. I verified the correspondence in the published text for Theorem 1.5, Remark 1.6, Proposition A.1, Theorem A.5 ('(Theorem 3.6(1))') and Theorem A.7 ('(Theorem 3.6(2))'). Giving both numbers in every locator is more work than the job requires and makes the file checkable against either version.

Coverage is complete: all 43 numbered statements appear in an item locator.

Statuses. The single library item cites Polynomial, RatFunc, LaurentSeries and Polynomial.Monic, all present in Mathlib at the pinned commit 082e2d3. The three planned items cite FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.0, DrinfeldModulesAndTModules:DM.0/DM.2/DM.6 and PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.9; those and the source route's DM.8 all exist in data/atlas.json.

Routes. One Part II and one source route, both accepted; see the route verdicts.

Mistakes in the paper. All three recorded findings are confirmed verbatim in the source, and each is settled by the paper against itself: S^zeta_d(s) defined with exponent d beside S^Li_d(s) with exponent s (E1); the condition '(q-1) | k' on a coefficient where k is the function field and the divisibility must be on the summation index j (E2); and 'dim_w Z_w' where every other statement writes dim_k (E3).

One finding added. All three recorded findings are of one mechanical class - a symbol that cannot mean what it says - so I ran the neighbouring class exhaustively: for every '<word>~\ref{label}' citation in the source, compare the word with the environment carrying the label. There are 89 such citations and two mismatches. One survives into the version of record and is now E4: the appendix proof says 'It follows by Theorem A.4' (published numbering) of a statement printed 'Proposition A.4', which section 1.3 itself cites correctly as a proposition. The other is preprint-only - section 1.3 of arXiv v2 says 'See Theorem~\ref{P:product of sLbullet}' for Proposition 2.3.5, and the published version reworded that sentence to 'stated as Proposition 2.7' - so it is recorded here rather than as a finding, since the published text is correct. The same audit found no duplicate labels and no undefined references.

Verdict: accept.
